title: CloneRunConfig
description: The configuration record of one supervised cloning run (ADR-019 track 1, ADR-010 erratum A2): the teacher TrainingSet to imitate, the seeds, the model sizes and the cross-entropy settings of a Preview and a Battle network trained separately. Reviewed JSON in the repository, validated fail-closed and referenced only by the SHA-256 of its JCS bytes (CheckpointRecord.run_config_hash). Real values are integers in millionths (_micro) or billionths (_nano). d_model must be a multiple of n_heads and max_picks may not exceed max_team (reader rules, as in TrainingRunConfig).

lineage_id.description: Label of the lineage the cloned pair starts; both CheckpointRecords carry it.

format_id.description: The Showdown format the games are played in.

seeds.description: Every seed of the run. None is a default: a run is identified by this record's hash.

run_key.description: Names the run in the battle seeds, the team draws and each Episode's collection record.

init_preview.description: Seed of the Preview network's random initialisation.

init_battle.description: Seed of the Battle network's random initialisation.

learner.description: Seed of the learner's own generator (minibatch order).

model.description: Network sizes (ADR-010 section 3): configuration, never code constants. d_model must be a multiple of n_heads (a reader rule).

options.description: Optional network options (ADR-010 erratum A4 item 2). Absent keeps today's bytes, hashes and checkpoints. A named option is added by the ticket of the experiment arm that needs it; none is defined yet, so only an empty object passes.

teacher.description: The scripted policy to imitate and the one TrainingSet of its games (ADR-010 erratum A2).

behaviour_policy_id.description: The teacher's policy id, <name>@<commit>, as the TrainingSet manifest and its Episodes record it. A learned pair's id (policy:<hash>) is not a teacher.

training_set_hash.description: SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of the teacher TrainingSet manifest: the hash the checkpoint records list.

clone.description: Cross-entropy settings, shared by both roles.

epochs.description: Passes over the training part of the set.

holdout.description: The part of the set held back from training, chosen per Episode by a keyed hash of the Episode hash (the rule shape of ADR-015: HMAC-SHA256 over the Episode hash as 64 lower-case hex characters, first 8 bytes big endian as n, held back when n * 10^6 < ppm * 2^64). The key is a public value of this record, not a secret. An Episode's Preview and Battle decisions are held back together. ppm 0 holds nothing back.

key.description: The 32 bytes of the HMAC key, as 64 lower-case hex digits.

ppm.description: Share of Episodes held back, in parts per million; at most one half.

learner.description: Where the learner runs (ADR-010 section 4). A cuda run is not claimed to be bit-reproducible, and its hash differs from a cpu run's.

device.description: cpu, or cuda from the separate GPU environment (ADR-010 section 5.2); a missing device is refused, never replaced.

threads.description: Intra-op threads of the learner on cpu.

Encoder.description: Feature widths and scales of the encoder (ADR-010 section 3); part of encoder_version.

max_moves.description: Moves per Pokemon the encoder holds.

max_team.description: Pokemon per side the encoder holds.

max_picks.description: Team Preview positions an order names; at most max_team (a reader rule).

stat_scale.description: Divisor of a Pokemon's exact stats.

options.description: Optional encoder options (ADR-010 erratum A4 item 2). Absent keeps today's bytes, hashes and checkpoints. A named option is added by the ticket of the experiment arm that needs it.

candidate_features.description: ADR-022 tier A (ADR-010 erratum A5 items 2 to 4). Each damaging move part of a battle candidate also reads the rows of the engine's damage calculation on assumed opponent sets, which the Node side builds (PolicyQuery.candidate_features). Names the feature set; feature_set_hash is the identity hash the builder computes (mechanics config, assumed-set config, adapter format, reader, version manifest), so a pin bump or a config change is another set. Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format. A pair that sets it has a policy id with a features member. probe-damage/2 (ADR-022 erratum E-22.3) also carries threat, speed and priority arrays, which the encoder attaches to the own and foe tokens and to the slot parts.

candidate_matchup.description: ADR-022 tier B (ADR-010 erratum A5 item 1). Each move candidate also carries the engine-data type-chart cells of the move's type against the shown types of each opposing position and the ally, and a flag that the move's type is one of the user's shown types. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

candidate_target.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. Each move candidate also carries the token of the Pokemon in the targeted active slot (the engine's target location read through the player's own request and the reduced slots; none for an untargeted or spread move, the user itself, or an empty or fainted slot), which the Battle network gathers into the slot part. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.
